title: How To Pre-generate Specific DB configurations?
body:
- Operating system (distribution) and version: macOS (Mojave and above)
- DBeaver version: Community 7.2.1

- Database name and version: Snowflake

Hi,
I'm working to automate database connections for users, meaning that when a user opens his laptop - opens DBeaver - he'll see all the database connections ready on his Database Navigator list. This doesn't mean they'll work, as the user will need to receive username/password separately to access it.
I've noticed I can export Projects, but not DB navigator configuration. Is this something that can be done / how can this be done?
author: IgalTov

comments.body:
This should be the file you're looking for:
~/Library/DBeaverData/workspace6/General/.dbeaver/data-sources.json

@p91paul Thank you! unfortunately, it seems there's only a "workspace2" folder, with /Scripts inside it and doesn't have the General folder as mentioned.
I tried looking for data-sources.json directly, but it was not found.

@p91paul Funny enough, it works with Jamf's MDM solution Composer when capturing it, but still not found in that directory. It seems to be coming from the ROOT folder.
Thanks again!

satisfaction_conditions: Information about the location of database connection configuration files in DBeaver
A method to pre-configure database connections for distribution to users
Compatibility with deployment tools like Jamf's MDM solution

title: How to completely uninstall DBeaver on Mac
body:
#### System information: 
- macOS Catalina 10.15.6 (19G73)
- DBeaver version: 7.1.5

#### Describe your question:

I want to completely remove everything DBeaver related and start over fresh with a brand new install that will not remember any of my preferences, cache, history, settings, connections, drivers, etc.

How can I do this on Mac? I've tried a few routes and after I reinstall, I can tell on opening it again that not everything got removed (it'll remember connection info, theme, etc.).
author: jim256

comments.body:
If you need to cleanup all your local files/settings then you can simple delete directory `~/Library/DBeaverData`.
Don't forget to close DBeaver before that.
@serge-rider , thank you. I think this worked. After I did that, rebooted, and re-installed, the only thing that was still the same was that it was using the dark theme. Is that now the default?

On MacOS dark theme is default if you use dark theme in MacOS itself.
In any case you can change it in the Preferences->Appearance.

satisfaction_conditions: Instructions for completely removing all DBeaver data and settings on macOS
Explanation for any remaining settings after reinstallation
Guidance that works specifically for macOS

title: SSH certificate support in SSH tunnel
body:
Hi Team, 

I am using an SSH certificate to access my servers. But there is no option to add SSH certificate, in SSH tunnel tab there is an option to add public key but it only accepts private key file to authenticate. On selecting the certificate file, I am getting an error: 

 _Can't initialize tunnel
  Cannot establish tunnel
  Cannot establish tunnel
    invalid privatekey: [B@5ecde315_

On terminal I am able to ssh using:  **ssh -i id-cert.pub username@servername**

It would be really nice to have the feature embedded out-of-the-box.

Is there any workaround for this, as I am stuck.

Thanks in advance.
author: arghaya

comments.body:
Really a great feature to have. This will provide much more security to the SSH tunnelling.

@arghaya, thanks for sharing!!

I also could not find accurate solution from dbeaver, but following hack should help you solve the issue

execute the command from terminal

**ssh -i id-cert.pub -fNL 3308:localhost:3307  username@server.com**

In the above command 
1. replace 3308 for local port through which all requests should be served
2. 3307 is the port where service on remote server is listening

So after that in Dbeaver you can configure using localhost and port used for tunnelling.

satisfaction_conditions: A working method to establish SSH connections using certificate-based authentication
A workaround that allows database connections via SSH certificate authentication
Instructions that can be implemented immediately without waiting for feature implementation
A solution that leverages their existing SSH certificate setup

title: warn if simultaneous query started
body:
It confused me when I ran two long queries in two tabs, to the same database.
It says it's running but then it appears that one waits for the other to finish first?  With no hint that that's the case.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Ideally both queries would run simultaneously.  If not then at least a different state like "waiting for other query to finish" would be nice to display in the UI.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
See above.
Thank you.
author: rdp

comments.body: somewhere in preferences there's an option called something like "open a different connection for each editor", try to enable it!

Yes that does work ("Database -> Editors -> SQL Editors"), thanks!
It's surprising to me that this wouldn't be the default...
As it is today it's just confusing "why does it say fetching table data *forever* when I run this SQL query..." so it would be nice to either make it the default or have some other status shown ("waiting for connection that's being used in other tab...") to reduce the confusion...

satisfaction_conditions: A way to run multiple SQL queries simultaneously on the same database
Clear indication in the UI when a query is waiting for another query to complete
Guidance on relevant configuration settings that affect query execution behavior
Improved default behavior or clearer status messages to reduce confusion
